concepts.learning_objective: Explain why all expressions a ± b ± c ± d formed from the same numbers have the same parity.
Decide, using parity rules, whether an arithmetic or algebraic expression is always even.

topics.title: Pairs to make fours and Always, Sometimes, Never

concepts.learning_objective: Use the forms 4p and 4p + 2 to decide when the sum of two even numbers is a multiple of 4.
Apply the properties of divisibility of sums, multiples, factors and LCM to judge statements as always, sometimes or never true.

topics.title: What remains? Remainders in algebraic form

concepts.learning_objective: Write all numbers with a given remainder on division as an algebraic expression such as 5k + 3.
Find remainders of sums and numbers satisfying several remainder conditions without long division.
Use the remainders of place values on division by 9 to find the remainder of a number.
Apply the digit-sum tests for divisibility by 9 and 3, including finding missing digits.
Use the alternating pattern of place values to test divisibility by 11 and find the remainder.
Choose factor tests based on prime factorisation to check divisibility by numbers such as 24 and 44.
Compute the digital root of a number by repeatedly adding its digits.
Relate the digital root of a number to its remainder on division by 9.
Solve addition cryptarithms using carries and place value reasoning.
Solve multiplication cryptarithms using size limits and units-digit patterns.
